newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI SAYS LONRHO DEAL AWAITS EU NOD.
newsitem.headline: JCI SAYS LONRHO DEAL AWAITS EU NOD.

text.p: South Africa's JCI Ltd said on Thursday its planned purchase of 26.8 percent in British conglomerate Lonrho Plc was yet to gain the approval of the European Union.
Thursday's Zimbabwean Financial Gazette reported JCI chairman MZI Khumalo as saying the deal was sealed.
"Its done, it's sealed and it's going ahead. We have already acquired the shares and we will take delivery in November," Khumalo was quoted as saying in an interview.
JCI spokesman Marc Gonsalves said the company was concerned that the quote was taken in isolation and could have implied the deal had been approved by the EU.
"There been no developments in the last 10 days on this issue," he added.
"As we have already indicated, guaranteed finance is already in place and the company has also been investigating other options."
He said JCI believed that the concerns of the European Commission could be addressed and it remained confident that the deal would go ahead as announced.
JCI announced on July 2 it would buy a 26.8 percent stake in Lonrho previously held by Anglo's for around 2.5 billion rand.
